title: Formal presentation and differential comparison at a separable closed point
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $\mathfrak p\subset S$ a maximal ideal, $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$, and $F=S/\mathfrak p$ its residue field. Assume $F/k$ is finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Write $\widehat A=\varprojlim_r A/\mathfrak m^r$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then $A$ and $\widehat A$ are Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; the maximal ideal of $\widehat A$ is $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ and its residue field is $F$. There is a $k$-algebra section $\sigma:F\to\widehat A$ of the residue map and, for some $n\ge2$, a continuous surjection of $F$-algebras $F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]\twoheadrightarrow\widehat A$, where $F$ acts on $\widehat A$ through $\sigma$, with kernel $(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subseteq(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. A presentation means any such $k$-algebra section $\sigma$ together with any such surjection, for any $n\ge2$ and any generators $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ of its kernel; everything below holds for every presentation. For every presentation, $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A$, where $\Omega$ denotes Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], is the cokernel of $\widehat A^{\oplus s}\xrightarrow{(\partial f_j/\partial t_i)}\widehat A^{\oplus n}$. For any extension field $K/k$ containing an embedded copy $F\hookrightarrow K$, let $\mathfrak q$ be the kernel of $S\otimes_kK\to K$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar s\lambda$, and put $B=(S\otimes_kK)_{\mathfrak q}$. Then $B$ is Noetherian local, $A\to B$ is a faithfully flat local map [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], $\mathfrak mB=\mathfrak m_B$, $B/\mathfrak mB=K$, and $\widehat B\cong K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ as complete local $K$-algebras, using $F\hookrightarrow K$ on coefficients. The comparison respects the images of $t_i$, and the same Jacobian cokernel presents $\Omega_{B/K}\otimes_B\widehat B$. Tensor products of algebras use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tags 0C52 (lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra), 0C54 (lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring), 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat), 0C50 (lemma-change-fields-algebraic-unramified); completed differential comparison is the Jacobian-completion passage in curves.tex, Tag 0C4D, proof of the algebraically closed case, extended to a finite separable coefficient field (its differentials over k vanish).

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian, so the finitely generated $k$-algebra $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] to the (flat) identity map $S\to S$ and the prime $\mathfrak p$ shows that $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ is a Noetherian local ring, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$ and residue field $A/\mathfrak m=S/\mathfrak p=F$ ($\mathfrak p$ being maximal; localization is exact). Since $\mathfrak m$ is an ideal of the Noetherian ring $A$, its completion $\widehat A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. The completion-local-ring lemma [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] applied to $(A,\mathfrak m)$ says that $\widehat A$ is local, its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m\widehat A$, and $A/\mathfrak m=F\to\widehat A/\mathfrak m\widehat A$ is an isomorphism; and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] (with $I=\mathfrak m$, finitely generated) says that $\widehat A$ is $\mathfrak m\widehat A$-adically complete. Thus the first local and residue assertions of the item hold, and $\widehat A$ is a complete local $k$-algebra (through $k\to S\to A\to\widehat A$) with residue field $F$.

source.place: Tag 0C52, lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra (proof: completeness of the right hand side by Algebra Lemma 05GG lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), with Algebra Tags 00FN, 0316, 05GI and 05GG.

proof.text: By step 1, $\widehat A$ is a complete local $k$-algebra whose residue field $F$ is finite separable over $k$, so the residue-field section lemma [lem-trf-separable-residue-coefficient-section] supplies a $k$-algebra map $\sigma:F\to\widehat A$ with $F\xrightarrow{\sigma}\widehat A\to\widehat A/\mathfrak m\widehat A=F$ the identity. Choose generators $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ (images of generators of the finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak m$). By the universal property of power series over a complete ring [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] (with $\Lambda=F$, $T=\widehat A$, $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak m\widehat A$, $\alpha=\sigma$, $t_i=y_i$) there is a ring map $\Phi:F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]\to\widehat A$ equal to $\sigma$ on constants and with $\Phi(t_i)=y_i$; it is a map of $F$-algebras for the $F$-structure through $\sigma$, and it is continuous since $\Phi((t_1,\ldots,t_n)^r)\subseteq(\mathfrak m\widehat A)^r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] (case $\Lambda=F$), $R_0=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ is a Noetherian local ring, complete for $I=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Then $I\widehat A=(y_1,\ldots,y_n)=\mathfrak m\widehat A$, $\widehat A$ is $\mathfrak m\widehat A$-adically complete, hence Hausdorff (step 1), and $R_0\to\widehat A/\mathfrak m\widehat A=F$ is surjective because it restricts to $\mathrm{id}_F$ on constants; so $\Phi$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-source-surjective-mod-ideal]. Its kernel is finitely generated, say by $f_1,\ldots,f_s$, because $R_0$ is Noetherian. Finally the composite $R_0\xrightarrow{\Phi}\widehat A\to F$ sends a constant $c$ to $c$ and each $t_i$ to $\bar y_i=0$, so it is the constant-term map, whose kernel is $(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$; hence $\ker\Phi\subseteq(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. (This is the argument of Tag 0C52; the Cohen structure theorem with its unrelated coefficient ring is not needed once $\sigma$ is fixed.)

source.place: Tag 0C52, lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra, last paragraph of the proof (kappa[[x_1..x_n]] -> O^, x_i -> f_i, surjective by Algebra Lemma 0315 lemma-completion-generalities), with More Algebra Tag 0C34 lemma-lift-residue-field.

proof.text: If the presentation in step 2 has $n<2$, adjoin $2-n$ dummy variables and add them to the kernel generators. The quotient, section, continuity, and containment of the kernel in the variable ideal are unchanged, so we may and do take $n\ge2$.

For an arbitrary presentation chosen in the statement, the completed-Jacobian lemma [lem-trf-completed-jacobian-differentials] applies with the given finite-separable extension $F/k$, section $\sigma$, and generators $f_j$. Its explicitly defined map sends $e_i$ to the continuous differential $\widehat d(t_i)$ and identifies the Jacobian cokernel with $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A$; hence the differential clause holds for every presentation.

source.place: Tag 0C4D, Jacobian presentation in the algebraically closed proof, with the continuous finite-separable coefficient-field extension.

proof.text: Let $K/k$ be an extension field containing the specified $k$-embedded copy $\iota:F\hookrightarrow K$, and define $\mathfrak q$ and $B$ as in the statement. The evaluation map $S\otimes_kK\to K$ is surjective ($1\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda$), so $\mathfrak q$ is a maximal ideal with residue field $K$, and $\mathfrak q\cap S=\ker(S\to F\xrightarrow{\iota}K)=\mathfrak p$ since $\iota$ is injective. The field-extension base-change lemma [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] makes $S\to S\otimes_kK$ faithfully flat. A presentation $S\cong k[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/\mathfrak a$ gives $S\otimes_kK\cong K[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/\mathfrak aK[x]$, so $S\otimes_kK$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Localizing at $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] gives a flat local map $A\to B$ of Noetherian local rings, and the local-flat faithful-flat lemma [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective] upgrades it to faithfully flat. For the fibre: by exactness of $-\otimes_kK$ and of localization, $B/\mathfrak mB=\big((S/\mathfrak p)\otimes_kK\big)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}=(F\otimes_kK)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, where $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ is the kernel of $F\otimes_kK\to K$, $a\otimes\lambda\mapsto\iota(a)\lambda$. Since $F/k$ is finite separable, $F\otimes_kK$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-tensor-field-reduced] (with $L=k$, $K'=F$, $E=K$). It is a finite-dimensional $K$-algebra, so every prime of it is maximal (a domain finite over a field is a field), hence $(F\otimes_kK)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ has a unique prime ideal, which is therefore its nilradical, which is $0$ by reducedness (localization of a reduced ring is reduced). So $B/\mathfrak mB$ is a field, hence equal to the residue field $B/\mathfrak qB=K$ of $\mathfrak q$, i.e. $\mathfrak mB=\mathfrak qB=\mathfrak m_B$. Thus all local-flatness, maximal-ideal, and residue-field clauses hold.

source.place: Tags 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat, parts (1), (3), (4)) and 0C50 (lemma-change-fields-algebraic-unramified, proof: the fibre ring has dimension 0 and is reduced, hence a field; reducedness by Algebra Tag 030U).

proof.text: Apply the completion-presentation base-change lemma [lem-trf-field-extension-completion-presentation] to the chosen presentation, using the $k$-embedding $F\hookrightarrow K$. The inverse-limit computation identifies $\widehat B$ with $K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ as complete local $K$-algebras and preserves the images of all variables.

Finally apply [lem-trf-completed-jacobian-differentials] over the base field $K$ to the finite-type $K$-algebra $S\otimes_kK$, the maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$, and the local ring $B$. Its residue field is $K$, the identity extension $K/K$ is finite separable, and the canonical section $K\to\widehat B$ is the structural map. The transported presentation from step 6 therefore gives the same Jacobian cokernel for $\Omega_{B/K}\otimes_B\widehat B$, with the variable images identified as asserted.
